title: Library holds: a fair queue for popular books

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own library hold-queue design case and kata, examples, code, quiz and explanations; no text from any site, book or course.

scenario: Before exams, every student wants the same few printed notes from the department library. Design and code the hold system: a student borrows a free copy if there is one, otherwise joins a fair queue for that book; when a copy comes back it goes straight to the first student waiting.

clarifying_questions.q: Is the queue per book or per copy?
clarifying_questions.a: Per book: any returned copy goes to the first person waiting for that book.

clarifying_questions.q: Does the next person have to collect it?
clarifying_questions.a: For this kata the copy is handed over at once on return.

clarifying_questions.q: Can a student hold two copies of one book, or wait while holding one?
clarifying_questions.a: No: one copy or one place in the queue per book.

clarifying_questions.q: What if the person returning is not the holder?
clarifying_questions.a: Refuse with an error; nothing changes.

functional: Borrow a free copy or join the queue, reporting the position
Return a copy, handing it to the first in the queue
Show the queue for a book

non_functional.name: Cost
non_functional.target: O(1) to join, hand over and borrow (queue position may be O(queue))

entities.name: Book
entities.responsibility: Free copy count, the set of current holders, and the FIFO queue of members waiting.

entities.name: Library
entities.responsibility: Finds books, applies the borrow and return rules, and decides who joins the queue where.

entities.name: Driver (Main)
entities.responsibility: Parses commands and prints replies; no rules.

patterns.name: FIFO queue per resource
patterns.why: Fairness is exactly first-in, first-out; a deque gives O(1) join and hand-over.

patterns.name: Policy in one method (enqueue)
patterns.why: Where a member joins the queue is isolated in one method, so a priority rule later changes only that method.

diagram.alt: Class diagram: Library holds a map of book names to Book objects and a set of faculty; Book has a free count, a set of holders and a queue of waiting members.

data.source:
classDiagram
  class Library {
    books: Map~name, Book~
    faculty: Set
    borrow(book, member)
    giveBack(book, member)
    enqueue(book, member)
  }
  class Book {
    free: int
    holders: Set
    queue: Deque
  }
  Library o-- Book

kata.io_protocol:
| Command | Prints |
|---|---|
| `COPIES <book> <n>` | `<book>: <n> copies` |
| `BORROW <book> <member>` | `<member> borrows <book>`, `<member> waits for <book> (position <k>)`, `error: no book <book>` or `error: <member> already has or awaits <book>` |
| `RETURN <book> <member>` | `<member> returns <book>`, `<member> returns <book>, now with <next>`, or `error: <member> does not have <book>` |
| `QUEUE <book>` | `<book>: <names in order>` or `<book>: nobody waiting` |

Anything else: `error: bad command <line>`.

change_request.description: Faculty members need books for lectures. Add `FACULTY <member>` (prints `<member> is faculty`). A faculty member who joins a queue goes **behind any faculty already waiting but ahead of all students**.

tests.input:
COPIES OS 1
FACULTY prof
BORROW OS s1
BORROW OS s2
BORROW OS prof
QUEUE OS
RETURN OS s1
tests.expected:
OS: 1 copies
prof is faculty
s1 borrows OS
s2 waits for OS (position 1)
prof waits for OS (position 1)
OS: prof, s2
s1 returns OS, now with prof

tests.input:
COPIES OS 1
FACULTY f1
FACULTY f2
BORROW OS s0
BORROW OS s1
BORROW OS f1
BORROW OS f2
BORROW OS s2
QUEUE OS
tests.expected:
OS: 1 copies
f1 is faculty
f2 is faculty
s0 borrows OS
s1 waits for OS (position 1)
f1 waits for OS (position 1)
f2 waits for OS (position 2)
s2 waits for OS (position 4)
OS: f1, f2, s1, s2

rubric.criterion: Kata tests pass, including the faculty change.
Book owns its copies, holders and queue; Library owns the rules; the driver only parses.
Hand-over on return goes to the queue head; no member can hold and wait for the same book.
The faculty rule changes only where members join the queue.
Naming and clarity (AI feedback, advice only).

concept_checks.stem: One copy; aditi holds it; bilal then charu wait. aditi returns. Who has the book?
concept_checks.explanation: The returned copy goes straight to the head of the queue.

concept_checks.stem: Which structure gives O(1) join at the back and O(1) take from the front?
concept_checks.explanation: A deque supports both ends in constant time.

concept_checks.stem: After the change, the queue is [f1, s1, s2] with f1 faculty. Faculty f2 joins. What is the queue?
concept_checks.explanation: Behind waiting faculty, ahead of students.

concept_checks.stem: Why isolate 'where a member joins the queue' in one method?
options: A new priority rule then changes one method instead of every borrow path
concept_checks.explanation: Policy in one place keeps changes local.

follow_ups: Give the next member 24 hours to collect a held copy before it passes on.
Notify a member by SMS when the book is handed to them.
Cap a member at 3 books across the library.

revision_card.front: Hold queue for scarce copies: data structure, return rule, and where priority goes?
revision_card.back: Per book: free count, holders set, FIFO deque. Return: if queue non-empty, hand the copy to queue head, else free++. Priority (faculty) lives in the one enqueue method.
